nodes.text: OVERVIEW OF LYMPHOCYTE ENGAGER-RELATED TOXICITIES

General Principles • The risks associated with each agent vary significantly; therefore, clinicians should refer to the individual FDA-approved prescribing information and appropriate clinical trial protocols for guidance on toxicity management after initiation of lymphocyte engagers (eg, T-cell– engaging bispecific antibodies). Institutions administering these therapies should have clear, agent-specific protocols in place to facilitate timely management of severe reactions such as CRS, ICANS, and other toxicities. • Disease-specific NCCN Guidelines with recommendations for prophylaxis and management of lymphocyte-engager–related toxicities offer additional guidance and are referenced in this section where available.

nodes.text: CRS • CD3-based lymphocyte engager therapies carry a universal risk of CRS. • Patients at elevated risk for high-grade CRS or poor tolerance of CRS include those with high tumor burden, rapid tumor progression, high inflammatory markers (eg, ferritin, CRP), higher age, comorbidities, or rapid onset of CRS <4 hours from start of infusion. • Signs and symptoms may include fever, hypotension, tachycardia, hypoxia, and chills. CRS may be associated with cardiac, hepatic, and/ or renal dysfunction. Serious events may include hypotension, hypoxia, atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia, cardiac arrest, cardiac failure, renal insufficiency, and capillary leak syndrome. • CRS may occur as early as hours after infusion and as late as 10–15 days post-infusion; be aware of the typical onset for the specific product used. Typical time to onset: 1–3 days; typical duration: 7–8 days; however, may be longer for specific products. • CRS risk requires frequent monitoring and early intervention to prevent progression to severe or refractory CRS. • Due to risk of CRS, lymphocyte engager therapies may require inpatient initiation for monitoring, with transition to ambulatory settings dictated by patient tolerability. • Consider providing patients with one dose of oral dexamethasone 8–12 mg to take if needed for severe CRS (eg, fever, chills, rigors, difficulty breathing, feeling severely ill) at home prior to travel to Emergency Department if instructed to do so. • Prophylactic tocilizumab may be considered to reduce the risk of CRS (ie, in patients with MM prior to first dose of talquetamab-tgvs or teclistamab-cqyv). An FDA-approved biosimilar is an appropriate substitute for any recommended systemic biologic therapy in the NCCN Guidelines. • See ENGAGE-3 for CRS grading. For guidance on CRS management, refer to ENGAGE-3 and the FDA-approved prescribing information.

ICANS • ICANS is a CNS toxicity associated with lymphocyte engager therapy. • ICANS is characterized by neurologic deficits, often concomitantly with CRS. Transient neurologic symptoms can be heterogeneous and include encephalopathy, delirium, aphasia, lethargy, headache, tremor, myoclonus, dizziness, motor weakness, ataxia, sleep disorder (eg, insomnia), anxiety, agitation, and signs of psychosis. Serious events including seizures, depressed level of consciousness, as well as fatal and serious cases of cerebral edema have occurred. Typical onset occurs during step-up dosing. • Early intervention to prevent progression to severe ICANS is important. • See CART-8 for ICANS Assessment/Grading. For guidance on ICANS management, refer to ENGAGE-5 and the FDA-approved prescribing information.

fever_present.definition: True if the case records a fever (temperature of 38°C or higher).

hypotension_present.definition: True if the case records hypotension, whether or not vasopressors are given.

vasopressor_count_excl_vasopressin.definition: Number of distinct vasopressor agents given, not counting vasopressin.

oxygen_support.definition: Highest oxygen support the case records for hypoxia. low_flow = low-flow nasal cannula or blow-by. high_flow = high-flow cannula, face mask, non-rebreather mask or Venturi mask. positive_pressure = CPAP, BiPAP, intubation or mechanical ventilation. other = any other support.

icans_grade_recorded.definition: ICANS (neurotoxicity) grade as recorded in the case. none = no neurotoxicity.

car_t_product.definition: CAR T-cell product the patient received.

lymphocyte_engager_agent.definition: T-cell-engaging bispecific antibody (lymphocyte engager) the patient received.

next_dose_planned.definition: True if the case describes the planned dose after the toxicity (next dose). False if the case describes the dose that was being given when the toxicity occurred (current dose).

disease_type.definition: Underlying malignancy treated with the lymphocyte engager or CAR T-cell therapy.

other_toxicity_grade.definition: Grade of a toxicity other than CRS or ICANS, as recorded in the case.

iec_hs_present.definition: True if the case states immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome (IEC-HS).

iec_hematotoxicity_prolonged_cytopenia_p.definition: True if the case states immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT) or prolonged cytopenias.

infection_or_hypogammaglobulinemia_prese.definition: True if the case states an infection or hypogammaglobulinemia after cell therapy.

iec_parkinsonism_present.definition: True if the case states immune effector cell-associated parkinsonism.

iec_cranial_nerve_palsy_or_polyradiculon.definition: True if the case states immune effector cell-associated cranial nerve palsy or polyradiculoneuritis.

guideline_section.definition: Which disease or subtype section of this guideline the case belongs to: the disease named in the guideline's page headings that the patient has (e.g. the tumor type or subtype).

hypotension_requiring_vasopressor.definition: Hypotension that requires a vasopressor, with or without vasopressin.

hypotension_requiring_multiple_vasopress.definition: Hypotension that requires multiple vasopressors, excluding vasopressin.

crs_grade.definition: Cytokine release syndrome grade from fever, hypotension, vasopressor need and oxygen support. none = no CRS.

crs_present.definition: True if the patient has cytokine release syndrome of any grade.

icans_present.definition: True if the patient has ICANS (neurotoxicity) of any grade.

notes.predicates: Conditions were drafted and reviewed by a language model (model_reviewed), not by clinicians. 'rejected' means the review rejected the draft; the box then needs clinician judgement. 'section_only' means the box only requires the patient to be in the page's guideline section.
notes.coordinates: bbox and line_bboxes are PDF points with the origin at the page's top left; pages[].size gives the page size.
notes.links: page links name a page id from pages[]; a multi-page code such as PROS-F has ids 'PROS-F 1 of 5' ... ; external_guideline links name another guideline's slug.
